# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [date you are sending this letter]

**To:** Wellpoint — Appeals Department
[appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Harper Kimura
Member ID: W631917869
[my mailing address]
[my phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-15 — Reference number POC-B70A1741F9-18248**
**Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
**Plan:** Wellpoint (Commercial/ACA), New Jersey
**Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the cervical fusion (ACDF) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 15, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Wellpoint to reconsider that decision, because the records already in my file match the plan's own published criteria in the guideline named above. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice, which says the appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 11, 2027**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. (Wellpoint/Anthem appeals are state- and plan-specific; members can also log in at anthem.com or through the Sydney Health app, or call the number on the back of the ID card.)

---

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

### 1. Imaging must correlate with the clinical findings

The plan's guideline states:

> "All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

My MRI of the cervical spine, performed on July 18, 2026, shows **C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression.** My clinical findings match that imaging: I have radicular pain and numbness into my **right thumb and index finger, with weakness**, and my exam documents **positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.** The side, the level, and the nerve distribution line up. This is the correlation the policy asks for. The imaging report is in the prior authorization packet and was interpreted by [name of the radiologist who read and signed the 2026-07-18 MRI, per the report].

The denial does not identify any specific imaging finding it found lacking, and it does not point to any competing radiology interpretation. If the reviewer relied on a reading that differs from my radiologist's report, the policy language above states that the radiologist report supersedes, and I ask that the report be applied.

### 2. The nerve root compression pathway

The plan's guideline states:

> "When imaging studies demonstrate nerve root compression due to herniated disc or spondylotic osteophyte correlating with the distribution of signs and symptoms, and ANY of the following criteria apply:"

My MRI demonstrates nerve root compression due to a disc herniation (C5-C6 disc herniation with C6 nerve root compression), and it correlates with the distribution of my signs and symptoms as described above. That excerpt ends in a colon and introduces a list of further conditions that was not reproduced in the material I have. Of the listed conditions I do have, two are met by my records:

> "Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement"

My records document a **neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level**, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and numbness and weakness in the right thumb and index finger — objective findings that correlate with the C6 impingement seen on MRI.

> "Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)"

My radicular pain has persisted for **nine months and is progressive and unrelieved by rest.** I completed **12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 20 visits, from April 12, 2026 to July 5, 2026**, including cervical traction and postural training, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is more than the six weeks this criterion names, and my pain did not resolve.

I am not asking the plan to apply the myelopathy, cord-compression, spondylosis-angulation or synovial-cyst pathways listed elsewhere in the guideline, and my records do not address them. My request rests on the nerve root compression pathway above.

### 3. Conservative management

The plan's guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

I completed physical therapy (20 visits over 12 weeks, with cervical traction and postural training) **and** more than one complementary strategy: **NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief**, and a **corticosteroid injection on April 27, 2026, which gave only two weeks of partial relief.**

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

The course above was completed for this episode of care and is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My symptoms are documented as **progressive over nine months and unrelieved by rest.** The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief and the injection gave two weeks of partial relief. After a full course of conservative care, I did not significantly improve.

### 4. Pain and functional impairment

The plan's guideline states:

> "significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs"

My records document ongoing pain, numbness and weakness in my right hand. To make the record complete against this definition, I am providing: pain rating [my current pain score out of 10, as recorded in my chart or by my surgeon] and the specific activities I cannot perform [list the daily activities I am unable to do — for example, specific self-care, household or work tasks — as documented in my chart]. My treating office can supply the corresponding chart note on request.

### 5. Surgical risk factors

The plan's guideline states:

> "Tobacco cessation. Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to spinal surgery is strongly recommended to reduce the risk of pseudoarthrosis."

I am a **non-smoker**. My records also document **no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.**

### 6. A request about the criteria actually applied

The plan's guideline states:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

That sentence introduces a list of required components that was not reproduced in the policy text available to me. If any required component was considered missing from my submission, I ask Wellpoint to identify it specifically so my surgeon's office can supply it. I also want to note plainly, for the reviewer's benefit, that I have quoted only the guideline language above; the denial notice itself did not quote any policy criterion to me, and it did not state which specific criterion my imaging failed to meet.

---

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Wellpoint to:

1. **Overturn the denial dated August 15, 2026 (reference POC-B70A1741F9-18248)** and authorize CPT 22551 as requested by Dr. Lindqvist.
2. If the denial is maintained, **identify in writing the exact criterion from the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon) that my records do not meet**, and state what documentation would satisfy it.
3. Provide me with a **copy of the full clinical criteria used in this review** and the **credentials and specialty of the reviewer** who made the determination.
4. Confirm my right to a further level of appeal, including external review, if this appeal is not resolved in my favor.

I am willing to have my surgeon's office send any additional records you need, and my surgeon is available for a peer-to-peer discussion. Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further is required.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

**Harper Kimura**
Member ID: W631917869

Progressive or severe neurologic deficits secondary to spinal cord or foraminal compression
